A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mutual-learning VPR framework, renamed from MVC-VPR to MutualVPR. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 has no appendices; v3's Appendices A and B are readable and included in this assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, viewpoint-clustering accuracy, augmentation robustness and clustering/backbone ablations in Tables 2–7.

after.justification: v3 reports retrieval and occlusion experiments, cropping and cluster-number ablations, and original descriptor/clustering analyses in Section 3 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The UTM/K-means mutual-learning loop, DINOv2/MulConv encoder, GeM projection, LMCL and retrieval inference remain intact. A limited reported model revision concerns adapter scale s: v1 specifies s=0.2, whereas v3 Section 4.1 describes it as learnable. Renaming the existing iterative clustering as adaptive clustering does not establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds MSLS-val retrieval evaluation and a dedicated severe-occlusion scenario using SF-XL-Occlusion's 76 queries. MSLS also appears in the added SALAD+CM training configuration. The original four retrieval benchmarks remain, including Pitts250k despite its omission from v3's appendix statistics table. GSV-Cities was already used by v1's baselines.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table 2, v3 Table 1 adds evaluated GeM, AnyLoc, ConvAP, BoQ, SALAD and SALAD+CM comparators. It also distinguishes original batch-interacting CricaVPR, a single-query variant and its PCA version. Conversely, the DINOv2/CricaVPR viewpoint-accuracy comparison and hierarchical/spectral clustering comparisons disappear with their respective analyses.

E3.justification: v3 introduces 0°, 30° and combined panorama-cropping conditions, producing six or twelve views, and adds R@10/R@20 evaluation for occlusion. NetVLAD changes from Pitts250k-trained, 32,768-dimensional descriptors to GSV-Cities-trained, 131,072-dimensional descriptors; other comparators receive reduced-dimensional configurations. The sampling description changes from one-fifth of the training set per epoch to one-fifth of classes within the selected group. These reported changes preclude treating all updated scores as same-setting gains.

E4.justification: v3 adds cropping-versus-label-supervision ablations, dedicated occlusion testing, t-SNE diagnosis of supervision inconsistencies, a reassignment case study and adjacent-class feature-distance analysis. It removes v1's augmentation-based viewpoint-accuracy study, Pitts250k viewpoint-classification examples, clustering-algorithm comparison and backbone efficiency study. The cluster-number ablation remains.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 and Figure 6 newly summarize feature-distance distributions with boxplots showing central tendency and spread. This is sample-distribution reporting, not uncertainty across training runs. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for retrieval performance.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive results, including 47.4% R@1 on SF-XL-Occlusion versus 40.8% for CricaVPR's single-query variant and SALAD+CM. Main-table SF-XL R@1 changes from 77.0 to 80.8 alongside changed cropping conditions. In the retained original-data cluster-number ablation, ResNet50 K=1 R@1 changes from 54.3 to 68.3 on Tokyo24/7 and from 30.3 to 52.1 on SF-XL without an explained cause. Several viewpoint-accuracy and efficiency result sets are removed.

T1.justification: The geographical-grid and clustered-label definitions and transformer/adapter equations are retained, with reordered numbering and equivalent notation. Neither version provides formal convergence guarantees, theorems or proofs. v3's new semantic-consistency arguments are qualitative interpretations rather than new mathematical results.

C1.justification: v3 extends the existing viewpoint-supervision claim to occlusion-driven inconsistencies and semantically aligned pseudo-label correction. Its abstract and contributions drop v1's headline near-perfect viewpoint-partitioning claim and low-space/high-efficiency contribution, emphasizing occlusion robustness and generalization instead. Mutual reinforcement and orientation-label independence remain central.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations based on correcting supervision errors, preserving semantic continuity across adjacent directions and retrieving occluded queries despite misclassification. It also introduces interpretations concerning EigenPlaces' generalization and CosPlace overfitting under cropping. v1's pitch-related difficulties, backbone generalization discussion and resource tradeoffs are removed. The fixed-K limitation and proposed dynamic-K future work are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses Adam, cosine annealing, learning rates of 1e-5 and 1e-2, and 50 epochs of 10,000 iterations, and adds panorama-cropping instructions and a code-access link. These disclosures do not establish increased training budgets. Conversely, v1's explicit adapter bottleneck/channel dimensions, N=5 setting and details accompanying the removed backbone/resource study are omitted.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands engagement with SALAD, BoQ, Clique Mining, GCL, AnyLoc and Divide&Classify, among other added references. It shifts the critique of EigenPlaces from dependence on spatial-distribution assumptions toward failures of common-reference-point similarity under occlusion. AP-loss, Multi-Similarity loss and Hungarian-method references are removed alongside their associated discussion or analyses.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the paper and updating authorship, v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work and interpretation. It adds a standalone Problem Analysis section, divides related work into two categories, reorganizes the method and structures experiments around three research questions. Dataset documentation moves into Appendix A.

P2.justification: The two-column layout becomes single-column, and the overview and framework diagrams are substantially redrawn. v3 adds supervision-diagnostic, reassignment and distance-distribution figures while removing v1's Pitts250k classification montage. Benchmark and supervision-ablation tables are expanded or restructured, several analysis tables disappear, and dataset statistics move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical assessability and reproducibility through broader comparisons, reduced-dimensional baselines, dedicated occlusion testing, controlled cropping comparisons and explicit optimization settings. The gain is limited by removal of v1's direct clustering-accuracy and efficiency studies and by overgeneralized interpretations. For example, Table 3 shows that cropping improves ResNet50 SF-XL R@1 by 16.3 points for CosPlace but only 0.3 for MutualVPR, qualifying the text's blanket claim that MutualVPR gains more.
